venue.name: TNT Paintball
venue.description: TNT Paintball is an outdoor paintball field on East Sooke Road, about half a kilometre along East Sooke Road from Rocky Point Road. It has six themed playing fields ranging from about half an acre to three acres, plus covered shelters with benches and tables where groups eat between games. Games run 15 minutes at a time with short breaks, and groups usually rotate through several fields. The published minimum age is 10 for regular paintball and 8 for the slower Splat Ball games, which use spring powered markers and smaller paintballs at about half the speed.

facility_notes.lunch_space: We have covered shelter with benches and tables. The shelters are quite large so often there may be several groups sharing one large shelter.

restrictions: The minimum age to play is 10 years old for both .50 and .68 calibre paintball, however we suggest a minimum of 12 years old for .68 calibre.
ALL paintballs must be purchased from TNT Paintball, no exceptions.
We are a FPO (Feild Paint Only) facility. Outside paintballs are not permitted.
You are welcome to bring any food or beverages along with you, but no alcohol whatsoever please.
We do not have permanent power at our facility and therefore are unable to have a fridge or freezer, so bringing an ice-cream cake is not recommended.
Sturdy footwear is a must. Shorts and tights are not recommended.
Everyone playing must complete a waiver.
venue.hours_notes: We are open year round and our normal operating hours are Saturdays and Sundays between 11:00 and 4:00. We are also available for group bookings on most weekdays with times being somewhat more flexible.
venue.seasonal_notes: Open year round, including holidays for weekday group bookings.

programs.name: Kid's Splat Ball private group
programs.description: Splat Ball uses spring powered markers and smaller paintballs that travel at about half the speed of a normal paintball, so the hit is much lighter. Kids between 8 and 12, along with parents and older siblings, make up the group of ten. Everyone gets a mask, a chest protector and a Splat Ball marker, and 2,000 paintballs are included for the group to share. Sessions run about 2.75 hours including sign up and instructions. Six players is the absolute minimum, and extra players beyond the first ten cost $25 plus tax each with no extra paintballs. Sixteen is the total maximum. All Splat Ball parties are private unless special arrangements are made. Booking goes through the Book Now button, choosing the Small Private session and then the Splat Ball option.
programs.what_children_do: Put on a mask and chest protector, get shown how the marker works, then play short games against each other across the wooded fields, walking between fields and sitting under a covered shelter for snacks in the breaks.
programs.our_note: This is the only thing here that works for primary age children, and it still starts at 8, so daycares and the youngest grades are out. The price is for the whole group of up to ten, not per child, which makes it cheap per head if you fill it and expensive if you do not.
programs.practical_summary: The whole visit is outdoors on wooded fields, with covered shelters, benches and tables for eating and a snack counter on site. Washrooms, wheelchair access, bus parking and what happens in heavy rain are not stated anywhere, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: The $449 covers a group of up to 10 and includes 2,000 paintballs. Extra players cost $25.00 plus tax each with no paintballs included. Extra paintballs are $8.93 per 100, $40.18 per 500 or $142.86 per 2,000, all plus tax.
programs.payment_timing: Parties must be booked in advance and are subject to availability.
programs.evidence: Group of up to 10 participants $449 (plus tax).

programs.name: Small private group paintball
programs.description: A private weekend session of 2.75 hours with 2,000 paintballs included for the group to share. Rental gear covers up to 10 players and 6 is the minimum needed to book. Extra players cost $35 plus tax each with no extra paintballs, up to a total of 16. Two start times are offered on most Saturdays and Sundays, 10:15 and 1:30, and the session books online through the Book Now buttons. Regular paintball is played in .50 or .68 calibre and the published minimum age is 10, with 12 suggested for the heavier .68 calibre.
programs.what_children_do: Get kitted out with a marker, mask and camouflage top, watch the safety video, then play 15 minute games across the themed fields with referees on the field and short breaks in between.
programs.our_note: The $549 buys the session for the group, not a place per child, so the cost per head depends entirely on how many you bring. Ten is the number the price is built around, and the minimum age of 10 rules out primary classes.
programs.practical_summary: Everything happens outdoors across six wooded fields, with covered shelters and tables for eating and snacks for sale. Nothing is published about washrooms, wheelchair access, bus parking or wet weather, so ask when you call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Extra players above the first 10 are $35 plus tax each and bring no extra paintballs. More paintballs are $8.93 per 100, $40.18 per 500 or $142.86 per 2,000, all plus tax.
programs.payment_timing: Prepaying for packages in advance is the only sure way of reserving your spot.
programs.evidence: We offer small private group sessions lasting 2.75 hours with 2,000 paintalls included to share among the group for $549 plus tax.

programs.name: Large private group paintball
programs.description: A private weekend session for a group as large as 60. The price is per player and rental gear is included for everyone, but paintballs are extra and can be bought in advance or on the day. At least 20 players have to be prepaid. These larger private games cannot be booked online and have to be arranged by phone on 250-658-1177. The published minimum age for regular paintball is 10.
programs.what_children_do: Play 15 minute games across the six themed fields, rotating from one field to the next so nobody waits, with breaks under the covered shelters.
programs.our_note: This is the one priced per person rather than per booking, so it is the option that scales for a large year group. Twenty prepaid players is the floor, and you have to phone rather than book online.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoor fields with covered shelters, tables and a snack counter, and gear included in the price. Washrooms, accessibility and bus parking are not stated, and a large group arriving by coach should check the road access first.
programs.extra_fees_note: Paintballs are not included. They are $8.93 per 100, $40.18 per 500 or $142.86 per 2,000, all plus tax, and must be bought from TNT Paintball.
programs.payment_timing: A minimum of 20 players must be prepaid.
programs.evidence: The cost is $37 plus tax per player with a minimum 20 players needed to be prepaid.

programs.name: Weekday group booking
programs.description: TNT is normally open at weekends, but a group can open the field on a weekday, holidays included. Sessions run up to four hours. The per player prices are the same as the regular games, but the field will not open unless a group of up to 10 is booked and paid in advance. You can bring as few as 6 players, but the group still has to prepay $321.43 plus tax for the whole group. Other members of the public may then join that day unless you pay a flat $50 plus tax to keep the session private. Available days and times are shown through the Book Now buttons, or by calling 250-658-1177.
programs.what_children_do: Play a run of 15 minute games on several of the six wooded fields, moving between fields with short breaks and a longer stop for food in a covered shelter.
programs.our_note: Weekdays are the only realistic window for a school group, and the catch is that the field will not open unless you prepay for ten places even if you bring six children. Budget the flat $50 on top if you want the field to yourselves.
programs.practical_summary: Outdoors on wooded fields with covered shelters and tables for lunch, and a snack counter on site. Washrooms, wheelchair access and bus parking are not stated anywhere, so call before you commit a class.
programs.extra_fees_note: $321.43 plus tax ($360 with tax) is the minimum the group must prepay to open the field, covering up to 10 players. Making the day private costs a further $50 plus tax. Paintballs are extra at $8.93 per 100, $40.18 per 500 or $142.86 per 2,000, plus tax.
programs.payment_timing: we need an initial group of up to 10 players booked and paid in advance to open the facility and book staff
programs.cancellation_note: If you are joining a public game as individual players, if the core group cancels and there are not enough other players left to open that day, we may need to cancel your booking. A full refund will be given.
programs.evidence: we still need the group of up to 10 prepaid at $321.43 plus tax ($360 w/tax) for the group to cover our costs

gaps: MINIMUM AGE: 10 years for regular paintball and 8 years for Splat Ball. That rules out daycares and preschools entirely, and the youngest primary grades.

The site never mentions schools, school groups or field trips. It names youth groups, church groups, social clubs, sports teams and birthday parties, so whether a school class would be taken is not stated. No school or youth rate is published.
WASHROOMS: not mentioned anywhere on the site, which matters at a rural outdoor site with no permanent power.
How many adults have to come with a group of children is not stated anywhere.
Bus parking and coach access are not stated. The directions describe a rural road and a yellow gate, and the site warns that online maps put its pin in the wrong place.
Wheelchair and stroller access are not addressed anywhere on the site.
What happens in heavy rain is not stated. There are covered shelters for between games, but play itself is outdoors.
The prices carry no year or season on the page. Two of the pages have 2017 in their web addresses, so the youth and birthday material may be older than the price page.
The address is given as 4590 East Sooke Road with no town or postal code. The map link on the site publishes coordinates, which is what was recorded.
The booking system sits on an outside website (vantora.com) rather than on the venue's own domain, so nothing there was read.
The site has no social preview picture, so the main picture was taken from the Splat Ball page instead. None of the photographs carried alt text and none had a credit line.

COORDINATES: their map and directions page has a Google map embed and a link through to Google Maps, and both give only the centre of the map view. Neither carries a pin on the site itself. The point we had, 48.34658 and -123.59183, was that view centre. It has been cleared. This matters more here than in town, because the address is a rural road with no town or postal code on it, so the entrance is worth confirming when you book.
